channel.title: EcoCompute — Notes
channel.description: Evidence-based notes on the energy cost of LLM inference, from direct NVML GPU power measurements.

item.title: Energy and quality, measured in the same run
item.description: Ten RTX 4090 configurations whose decode energy and perplexity come from the same run (direct NVML, n=1 each). NF4 saves 39% energy at 7B but costs 12% perplexity; INT8 costs about 0.5% perplexity and never saves energy. A delta-perplexity filter of 1% rejects every NF4 row and admits nearly every INT8 one, inverting the energy ranking. Also reports a 2.0-2.5x cross-session discrepancy in the INT8 penalty on the same card model and software stack. Data: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22019742.

item.title: EcoCompute 容器数据测量 · 中文使用手册 / Chinese-language container how-to

item.title: We ran our own container on a rented RTX 4090: NF4 breaks even just above 3B, INT8 lost at every size we tested
item.description: 15 of 15 configurations measured with direct NVML on a rented RTX 4090 using our own open MLCube container. NF4 flips from a +36% penalty at 0.5B to break-even at 3B and a -28% saving at 7B; INT8 cost more energy at all five sizes tested (n=1 each, bitsandbytes LLM.int8()) because decode throughput collapses to 9-19 tok/s. Data archived at DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22019742.

item.title: When not to quantize: the small-model energy penalty
item.description: Weight-only NF4/INT8 quantization shrinks memory but can raise LLM inference energy by 25–55% for small models. What 360+ real GPU measurements show about the crossover point, and when quantization is still the right call.
